items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There was a tenor saxophone player whose name was Bumps Myers. The lead trombonist, a wonderful lead trombonist, a little dude.

ctx.x: There was a tenor saxophone player whose name was Bumps Myers. The lead trombonist, a wonderful lead trombonist, a little dude. In order to be seen he had to sit on a stack of telephone books in the orchestra. What was his name? [John "Shorty" Haughton] He was a wonderful player. He could do the Tommy Dorsey style approach to ballads beautifully. I can’t think of his name.
I know it and can’t think of it either.
